sentences.text: 5. Offences added, if any -- 6. Date of passing of impugned 13.10.2023 order 2.
It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that there was delay in lodging the FIR and parties have entered into compromise.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that after investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
However, learned counsel for the complainant candidly admit the fact of compromise entered between the parties and does not oppose if bail is granted.
4. Have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.

Taking into account the submissions that there is an inordinate delay in lodging of the FIR and the genesis of the occurrence has been suppressed as well as considering the submission that after lodging of the FIR, the parties have entered into compromise and today neither the victim nor her family members deserve to keep the petitioner behind the bars.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
It is also observed that if the victim is declared hostile in the trial then, it would be a futile exercise, thus, keeping the petitioner behind the bars would not justifiable.

On the ground of parity [2023:RJ-JD:39322] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-13609/2023] and on the ground that the trial would still take a long time to conclude, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
Needless to say, none of the observations made herein under shall affect the rights of either of the parties during trial and this Court refrains from commenting on the niceties of the matter.

5. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARZAND ALI),J 477-amit/-
